memory_update.text: SOLS should be added to the nuclear fuel-cycle discovery lane because its Metropolis Works UF6 conversion facility appears to be a direct, underfollowed U.S. conversion chokepoint hidden inside a specialty-materials spin-off.
LEU remains a core reference candidate for HALEU enrichment because of DOE task-order selection and existing HALEU demonstration production.
FLR should be tracked as an EPC execution-capacity candidate tied to X-energy/Dow Seadrift, but evidence must verify conversion from front-end engineering to full EPC backlog.
Nuclear bottleneck mapping should separate uranium conversion, enrichment/HALEU, fuel fabrication, qualified components, and EPC execution; these may tighten independently.
Qualified component suppliers such as BWXT and Curtiss-Wright need a separate follow-up pass; current candidate limit prioritized fuel-cycle and EPC exposure.

summary: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe around the nuclear-fuel and execution bottleneck. The strongest direct exposure appears in HALEU enrichment, UF6 conversion, advanced fuel fabrication, and EPC/project-execution capacity rather than only in headline reactor developers. Two lanes are retained: reference names that define the node and an underfollowed discovery lane where nuclear exposure is embedded in specialty materials or diversified engineering labels.
